title: Four rolls for one six
hook: Each roll has a 1 in 6 chance of a six. What do four rolls give you?

knows: one roll of a fair die gives a six with chance 1/6
doesNotKnow: how chances combine over repeated tries
the complement trick: count the ways to miss every time

misconception: Four rolls, each 1/6, so the chance of at least one six is 4/6 (67%).
objective: The learner can explain that each roll removes 1/6 of those still without a six, so the no-six share is (5/6)^4 = 48% and at least one six is 1 - (5/6)^4 = 52%, not 4/6.
keyState: All four rolls done: the no-six bars 1,000 -> 844 -> 701 -> 581 -> 477, above the dashed adding line (333 at roll 4).

claims.text: Each roll of a fair die gives a six with chance 1/6.
The chance of at least one six in four rolls is 1 - (5/6)^4 = 51.8%, about 52%.
The stage's 1,000 seeded players went 1,000 -> 844 -> 701 -> 581 -> 477 with no six, so 523 (52%) had at least one six after four rolls.
claims.source: players() and stillNoSix() in model.ts, mulberry32 seed 1654, untuned (the first seed tried). Exact expected: 1,000, 833, 694, 579, 482. Over seeds 1-500 the no-six count after 4 rolls had middle 95% 454-512 (median 482).

claims.text: Adding 1/6 per roll predicts 333 players left with no six after four rolls (67% with a six), and would pass 100% by the seventh roll.
Each roll removes about 1/6 of the players still without a six, not 1/6 of everyone.
claims.source: Independence of rolls: the no-six group after r rolls is (5/6)^r of all players in expectation.

recall.question: A free throw goes in 50% of the time. Is the chance of at least one basket in two tries 100%?
recall.why: Missing both happens 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4 of the time, so at least one basket is 1 - 1/4 = 75%. Chances of tries do not add.
